meta.titre: World Forestry and Fishing Grounds: main regions, conditions for growth and threats to the resource
meta.sous_theme: Types and regions of forestry, fishing grounds of the world, their conditions and conservation

sections.contenu_markdown: From the forests of southern Cameroon, logs travel to the port of Douala and on to Europe and Asia. In the cold north Atlantic, trawlers from several countries fish on a shallow bank, and in Canada millions of pine and spruce trees feed paper mills. The GCE paper wants to know where the main forests and fishing grounds of the world are, and why. Learning a handful of precise places and the reasons behind them is enough to answer most questions.

items: Plankton are tiny living things in water that fish eat.
A continental shelf is the shallow gently sloping sea floor around a continent.
A climate with long cold winters supports different trees from a hot, wet climate.

sections.titre: Where the world's timber and fish come from and why
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Forest regions
| Type | Where | Main features |
|---|---|---|
| Tropical rainforest | Amazon basin, Congo basin (including southern and eastern Cameroon), South-East Asia | Hardwoods such as mahogany, iroko, ayous and sapele; many species mixed together; hard to reach |
| Temperate forest | Eastern North America, Western Europe, north-eastern Asia | Mixed deciduous and coniferous trees |
| Coniferous (softwood) forest | Canada, Scandinavia, Russia | One or few species such as pine, spruce and fir in large stands; softwood used for paper pulp, building timber and furniture |

Softwood forests are easier to cut and process because trees of one kind grow together, and rivers can be used to float logs to the mills. Tropical hardwoods are valuable but cut selectively because many species are mixed.

### Fishing grounds
| Ground | Position | Main fish |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Banks | North-west Atlantic, off Newfoundland | Cod |
| North Sea | North-east Atlantic, between Britain and north-west Europe | Herring and cod |
| North-west Pacific | Off Japan and eastern Russia | Many species |
| North-east Pacific | Off Alaska and British Columbia | Salmon |
| Peru coast (southern hemisphere) | South-east Pacific, off Peru and Chile | Anchovy |

### Conditions for a good fishing ground
- A broad **continental shelf** with shallow water, where sunlight reaches through the water and plankton (the food of fish) grows well.
- The meeting of cold and warm currents, or upwelling of cold nutrient-rich water, which brings food to the surface.
- An indented coast with sheltered harbours, and a nearby market with good transport and cold storage.

### Threats and management
Overfishing and illegal logging reduce stocks and forest. Management measures: quotas on catches, larger net mesh, closed seasons, fish farming, replanting, selective logging and forest reserves.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to mark a forestry area or a fishing ground
variantes.contenu_markdown: Choose a named place in the right hemisphere. For forestry in temperate lands name Canada's coniferous belt or Scandinavia. For northern fishing grounds name the Grand Banks and the North Sea. Check the equator: Peru's anchovy grounds are in the Southern Hemisphere and cannot be used when the question says northern hemisphere.

variantes.nom: Explain why a fishing ground is rich
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is explain or account for the richness of a named ground
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give physical reasons first (shallow shelf, plankton, currents meeting), then human reasons (ports, markets, technology). Two or three well-explained reasons are better than a list of five.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain why the Grand Banks, off the coast of Newfoundland, are a rich fishing ground.

etapes.justification: Location sets the context of the answer.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The Grand Banks lie in the north-west Atlantic, off Newfoundland, on the continental shelf.

etapes.justification: The shallow depth lets sunlight reach the water, so plankton grows.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The water is shallow, plankton grows, and fish come to feed on it.

etapes.justification: Mixing of different waters brings nutrients and plankton.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The cold Labrador Current meets the warm Gulf Stream there, mixing the water and increasing the food supply.

etapes.justification: An explanation of richness is stronger when it also says why people have chosen to fish there.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Nearby ports and large markets in North America and Europe encouraged fishing.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The Grand Banks are in the north-west Atlantic off Newfoundland, on a broad, shallow continental shelf. Sunlight reaches the shallow water and plankton grows, and fish feed on it. The cold Labrador Current meets the warm Gulf Stream there, mixing the waters and increasing the supply of food. Nearby ports and large markets in North America and Europe have also encouraged fishing, although overfishing has reduced the cod stocks.

items.erreur_markdown: "Fishing grounds are found in the deepest parts of the ocean."
items.pourquoi_faux: Fish depend on plankton, which grows where sunlight reaches the water, so rich grounds lie over shallow continental shelves.
items.correction_markdown: Fishing grounds lie on continental shelves, where the water is shallow.

items.erreur_markdown: "Tropical rainforest produces softwood such as pine."
items.pourquoi_faux: Rainforests produce hardwoods. Pine and spruce are softwoods of cool, high-latitude forests.
items.correction_markdown: Tropical rainforest: hardwoods such as mahogany and iroko. Canadian and Scandinavian forests: softwoods.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Peru coast is a fishing ground of the Northern Hemisphere."
items.pourquoi_faux: Peru and its coast lie south of the equator.
items.correction_markdown: Choose a northern ground such as the Grand Banks or the North Sea when the question says Northern Hemisphere.

items.erreur_markdown: "Managing a fishing ground means banning all fishing for ever."
items.pourquoi_faux: Management aims at sustainable fishing: people may still fish, within limits that let the stock breed and recover.
items.correction_markdown: Use quotas, larger mesh nets and closed seasons so that fishing can continue without destroying the stock.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify these trees as hardwood or softwood: pine, mahogany, spruce, iroko, fir.

A logging company fells 5 trees per hectare over 1,200 hectares and must plant 3 new trees for every tree felled. (a) How many trees are felled? (b) How many must be replanted? (c) What is the cost if each young tree costs FCFA 350?

A fishing ground has a total allowable catch of 80,000 tonnes a year. Country X is allowed 30% of it, but lands 27,500 tonnes. (a) Calculate Country X's quota. (b) By how much did it exceed the quota? (c) The fish stock fell from 400,000 tonnes to 260,000 tonnes; calculate the percentage fall. (d) Name two measures to protect the stock.
items.solution_markdown: (a) 30% of 80,000 = **24,000 tonnes**. (b) 27,500 − 24,000 = **3,500 tonnes**. (c) Fall = 400,000 − 260,000 = 140,000 tonnes; 140,000 ÷ 400,000 × 100 = **35%**. (d) Quotas and closed seasons (also larger mesh nets or fish farming).

items_markdown: Tropical rainforests produce hardwoods and are cut selectively; coniferous forests of Canada, Scandinavia and Russia produce softwood.
Northern fishing grounds include the Grand Banks, the North Sea and the north-west and north-east Pacific; the Peru coast is in the Southern Hemisphere.
A rich fishing ground has a broad shallow shelf, plankton and mixing currents.
On a map question, name a specific place and check the hemisphere.
Conservation uses quotas, closed seasons, replanting, selective logging, reserves and fish farming.
